newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soymeal down as funds roll out of Dec.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soymeal down as funds roll out of Dec.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were mixed at midsession with nearbys down as funds rolled out of the December ahead of first notice day next Friday, traders said.
"There is a big long who needs to roll out of that position," one trader said. "Once this rolling is done, I think the Dec will come back to life."
On the fundamental side, traders said cash soymeal basis levels remained high and weekly crush totals were expected to again top 30 million bushels.
Talk that FOB soymeal basis levels in Brazil had slipped was pressuring U.S. export markets. Still, traders noted Brazil did not have much supply to ship at those levels.
"I think there's evidence from our soybean and meal export numbers that we are the only available source," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Soyoil was mostly lower in technical trade. Charts indicated initial support in December soybean oil at 23.16 cents per lb with resistance at 23.51.
At 1156 CST, soymeal was $2.40 per ton lower to $0.50 higher with December down $2.40 at $235.80. Soyoil was steady to 0.11 cent per lb lower with December unchanged at 23.29.
